description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, generously loaded with a medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. Its crispy edges and tender, flavorful interior make it an irresistible appetizer or a delightful light meal. This traditional dish perfectly balances textures and tastes, offering a true taste of Korean comfort food.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, minced garlic, and gochugaru (if using). Stir well and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Ensure your mixed seafood is thawed, cleaned, and chopped into bite-sized pieces. Wash and cut green onions into 2-3 inch lengths. Thinly slice the yellow onion and red chili pepper (if using).

instructions.title: Make the Pancake Batter
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, and sugar. Add the cold water and egg, then whisk until a smooth batter forms with no lumps. Be careful not to overmix.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Gently fold the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced yellow onion into the batter. Mix just enough to distribute the ingredients evenly without overworking the batter.

instructions.title: Cook the First Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil. Once hot, pour about half of the batter mixture into the pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Arrange some extra green onion pieces and sliced red chili on top if desired.

instructions.title: Flip and Cook Until Crispy
instructions.text: Cook for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Drizzle another tablespoon of oil around the edges, then carefully flip the pancake. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on the second side until it is also golden brown and the seafood is fully cooked through.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges or squares and serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat the cooking process for the remaining batter.

tips: For the crispiest Pajeon, use very cold water in your batter and ensure your pan is hot with enough oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Using a combination of all-purpose flour and rice flour gives the pancake a perfect balance of chewiness and crispiness. Do not skip the rice flour.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking to enjoy its best texture. It pairs wonderfully with Korean makgeolli (rice wine) or a cold beer.
article:
Discover the culinary delight that is Haemul Pajeon, a beloved Korean seafood pancake cherished for its crispy edges, tender interior, and abundance of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This savory pancake isn't just a dish; it's an experience, often enjoyed as a comforting snack, a hearty appetizer, or a perfect accompaniment to a glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine) on a rainy day. Whether you're a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or new to its rich flavors, learning about and making Haemul Pajeon offers a delicious journey into one of Korea's most iconic street food and restaurant staples.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon translates literally to "seafood green onion pancake," a name that perfectly encapsulates its primary components. At its heart, it's a crispy, pan-fried pancake studded generously with various seafood and long strands of green onions, all bound together by a light, savory batter. Unlike some other Korean pancakes (jeon), Haemul Pajeon is distinguished by its substantial texture and the prominent role of both the seafood and the green onions, which are often arranged decoratively before cooking. The magic lies in the contrast: a golden-brown, almost tempura-like crust giving way to a soft, chewy interior brimming with oceanic sweetness and the sharp bite of green onions. It’s a dish that perfectly balances freshness, texture, and flavor, making it incredibly satisfying.

## Ingredients for Authentic Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon requires a few key elements, most of which are readily available. The beauty of this dish is its flexibility, allowing you to tailor the seafood to your preference.

For the Pancake Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour
*   1/2 cup rice flour (for extra crispiness, optional but recommended)
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (helps with browning)
*   1/4 teaspoon black pepper
*   1.5 cups cold water or anchovy broth (broth adds depth of flavor)
*   1 large egg

For the Seafood and Vegetables:
*   1 bunch green onions (about 10-12 stalks), cut into 3-4 inch lengths
*   1 cup mixed seafood, chopped into bite-sized pieces. Popular choices include:
    *   Shrimp (peeled, deveined)
    *   Squid or calamari (cleaned, scored, and sliced)
    *   Mussels (cleaned, shelled)
    *   Oysters (cleaned)
    *   Clams (cleaned, shelled)
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional)
*   1-2 small red chili peppers, thinly sliced (for a touch of heat, optional)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon sesame seeds
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)
*   A few slivers of green onion

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Haemul Pajeon is simpler than you might think, yielding impressive results with a bit of attention to detail.

1.  **Prepare the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, sugar, and black pepper. Gradually add the cold water (or broth) and egg, whisking until a smooth, thin batter forms. It should be slightly thinner than pancake batter but thick enough to coat the ingredients. Avoid overmixing to prevent a tough pancake. Refrigerate the batter for at least 15-20 minutes, or even longer, as a cold batter helps achieve a crispier texture.

2.  **Prepare Seafood and Vegetables:** Thoroughly clean and pat dry all seafood. Cut shrimp, squid, or any larger pieces into bite-sized portions. Cut green onions into uniform 3-4 inch lengths. If using, slice the onion and chili peppers thinly.

3.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large, non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of vegetable oil – enough to coat the bottom of the pan and create a shallow pool (about 2-3 tablespoons). The oil is crucial for crispiness.

4.  **Assemble the Pancake:** Once the oil is hot (it should shimmer), arrange a layer of green onion pieces neatly across the bottom of the pan. Sprinkle the prepared seafood evenly over the green onions. You can also add sliced onions and chili peppers at this stage.

5.  **Pour the Batter:** Ladle a thin layer of the prepared batter over the seafood and green onions, ensuring everything is lightly coated and connected. Don't drown the ingredients in batter; the green onions and seafood should still be visible.

6.  **Cook and Flip:** Cook for 5-7 minutes on the first side, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges begin to set. To check for crispiness, gently lift an edge with a spatula. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges of the pancake if it looks dry. Once golden, carefully flip the pancake. This can be the trickiest part; a large, sturdy spatula or two spatulas can help.

7.  **Cook the Second Side:** Press down gently on the pancake with your spatula to ensure even contact with the pan. Cook for another 4-6 minutes, or until the second side is also golden brown and crispy, and the seafood is cooked through.

8.  **Serve:** Transfer the Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice into wedges or squares.

## Tips for the Crispiest Korean Seafood Pancake

Achieving that perfect, shatteringly crisp exterior is key to an exceptional Haemul Pajeon.

*   **Cold Batter:** Keep your batter chilled. Cold batter reacts better with hot oil, resulting in a crispier texture and less oil absorption.
*   **Plenty of Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil. Haemul Pajeon isn't deep-fried, but it needs a generous amount of oil for that signature crisp. You can drain excess oil after cooking.
*   **High Heat:** Start with medium-high heat. Too low, and the pancake will soak up oil and become greasy; too high, and it will burn before cooking through. Adjust as needed.
*   **Single Layer:** Cook one pancake at a time to maintain consistent heat and ensure even cooking. Overcrowding the pan lowers the temperature.
*   **Rice Flour:** Incorporating rice flour into your batter significantly enhances crispiness compared to using all-purpose flour alone.
*   **Pat Dry Seafood:** Excess moisture from the seafood can lead to a soggy pancake. Pat everything dry thoroughly before adding to the pan.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is typically served immediately after cooking, when it's at its crispiest and hottest. It's often cut into wedges or squares, making it easy to share.

The perfect accompaniment to Haemul Pajeon is a simple, tangy dipping sauce that complements its savory richness without overpowering it. To make the dipping sauce: combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and optional minced garlic, gochugaru, and green onion slivers. Stir well and serve alongside the warm pancake.

Haemul Pajeon pairs wonderfully with a cold beer, soju, or the traditional Korean rice wine, makgeolli. It's also a fantastic appetizer before a larger Korean meal or a satisfying light lunch on its own.

## Variations and Substitutions for Haemul Pajeon

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a star, its versatility allows for many delicious variations:

*   **Kimchi Pajeon (Kimchi Jeon):** For a spicy, fermented twist, add chopped kimchi to the batter. This is another incredibly popular Korean pancake.
*   **Vegetable Pajeon (Yachae Jeon):** If seafood isn't your preference, you can make a purely vegetable version by adding thinly sliced carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, or bell peppers.
*   **Meat Additions:** Some recipes include thinly sliced beef (bulgogi style) or pork alongside or instead of seafood for a more substantial pancake.
*   **Spicy Kick:** Increase the amount of red chili peppers or add a spoonful of gochujang (Korean chili paste) to the batter for extra heat.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Substitute the wheat flour with a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend and ensure all other ingredients are certified gluten-free.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Haemul Pajeon

**Q: Can I make Haemul Pajeon ahead of time?**
A: While best enjoyed fresh for maximum crispiness, you can prepare the batter and chop the ingredients in advance. Store them separately in the refrigerator. Cook just before serving. If you have leftovers, reheat them in a dry skillet or air fryer to regain some crispiness, though it won't be as good as freshly made.

**Q: What kind of seafood is best for Haemul Pajeon?**
A: A mix is generally best for flavor and texture variety. Shrimp, squid, and mussels are very common. Clams, oysters, or even scallops can also be used. Ensure all seafood is fresh and properly cleaned.

**Q: Is Haemul Pajeon spicy?**
A: Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon is savory, not spicy. However, thinly sliced red chili peppers are often added for a subtle kick and visual appeal. You can omit them entirely or add more for extra heat, or even serve with a spicy dipping sauce.

**Q: Why is my pancake soggy?**
A: Common reasons for a soggy pancake include not enough oil, not heating the pan sufficiently before adding the batter, overcrowding the pan, or using too much batter relative to the ingredients. Ensure your seafood is well-drained and patted dry.

**Q: What's the difference between Pajeon and Buchimgae?**
A: "Pajeon" specifically refers to a Korean pancake featuring green onions ("pa"). "Buchimgae" is a broader term for any pan-fried dish made with a batter, essentially meaning "Korean pancake." So, Pajeon is a type of Buchimgae.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a pancake; it's a celebration of fresh ingredients, balanced flavors, and comforting textures. With this guide, you’re well-equipped to recreate this Korean favorite in your own kitchen, bringing a taste of Seoul right to your table. Enjoy the process, and savor every crispy, savory bite!
